external_source: causaldata `thornton_hiv` (Thornton 2008), via NickCH-K/causaldata (MIT) — external anchor: 34% baseline pickup, any incentive roughly doubled it

local_attempt.outcome: no estimate produced — outright timeout failure
local_attempt.note: Causal effect estimation (propensity score matching / DiD) exceeded the 600s sandbox execution limit on both attempts; the adaptive retry loop's same-reason-stop guard correctly fired this time ('Same failure reason twice (Timeout) — stopping retries after 2 attempt(s)') and aborted the task rather than looping further. Only exploratory work survived: dataset load + sample constraint (N=100 of 4,820 rows), median/mode imputation, and five confounder/outcome visualizations (age, distance, HIV status, incentive amount vs. pickup). No ATE, no dose-response, no heterogeneity analysis — the report is explicit and honest about what failed ('critical execution failures... prevented the completion of core causal inference tasks'), unlike the confidently-wrong sign-flip failures seen elsewhere in this local-mode pass. This is a visible, self-reported failure, not a silent one. See notes.md.

estimate.note: GADS canonical from cloud reference run (drafted lane, DoWhy + multivariable IPW regression, village-clustered SEs): ATE = 0.4395 (95% CI [0.3973, 0.4817]) — closely consistent with the external anchor (34% baseline, roughly doubled by any incentive implies an effect in the same ballpark). Backed by unprompted extras: a dose-response analysis (+17.71pp per incentive unit) and heterogeneity analysis showing the effect is stronger for people living further from the testing center (distance x incentive interaction +0.0141) — a substantively sensible finding nobody asked for.
